edges.dependent: Queuing Delay, Packet Loss, and Statistical Multiplexing
edges.rationale: Queuing delay and packet loss occur in the output buffers of store-and-forward switches; understanding that packets are received, stored, and retransmitted per hop is needed before analyzing buffering, delay, and on-demand capacity sharing.
The comparison evaluates packet switching's per-hop store-and-forward behavior (transmission delays, no reservation), so the packet-switching mechanism must be understood first.

edges.prerequisite: Circuit Switching with FDM and TDM
edges.rationale: The trade-off analysis (reserved vs. on-demand bandwidth, wasted capacity during silent periods) presupposes knowledge of how circuits and FDM/TDM partition link capacity.

edges.prerequisite: Queuing Delay, Packet Loss, and Statistical Multiplexing
edges.rationale: The argument that packet switching suits bursty traffic rests on statistical multiplexing, and its drawbacks (queuing delay, packet loss under congestion) are key terms in the comparison.
